summary: UMAMI & KOJI LAB is a private, hands-on koji fermentation experience held in chef and author Chie Ando's Jingumae kitchen in Shibuya, Tokyo. Over about three and a half hours, guests inoculate steamed rice with tane-koji by hand, see koji-no-hana alive under a microscope, taste amazake, shio-koji and shoyu-koji side by side, and cook lunch with the seasonings. Sessions run in English with a bilingual assistant, are private for one to four guests, and can be prepared fully vegan. Every guest goes home with rice koji, an aged soy sauce kit, koji grains and a signed textbook. From ¥65,000 per person, tax included.

blocks.title: What is Koji?
body: Koji is Japan's national mold — the quiet soul behind miso, soy sauce, sake, and mirin. For over 1,000 years, it has lived in Japanese homes, transforming humble ingredients into something profound. Now, it lives in ours.
Koji is the heart of Japanese fermentation culture. It is used in many traditional foods.
Koji doesn't just ferment food. It ferments time itself.
In this intimate session, chef and author Chie Ando opens her Jingumae kitchen to share the science, the craft, and the living culture that makes Japanese food unlike anything else on earth.

blocks.title: Step Inside the Kitchen
blocks.videoTitle: One minute on koji — UMAMI & KOJI LAB, Tokyo
blocks.lead: One minute on koji itself — not on the lesson, not on us. Rice becoming sweetness, salt becoming depth, time becoming nourishment: a thousand years of careful hands, still at work in a modern Tokyo home.
blocks.note: On the day, a second film is waiting for you — a full explanation, narrated in English, that takes you far deeper into the world of koji and fermentation.

blocks.title: Three and a half hours, step by step
blocks.lead: Serious fermentation, in a kitchen the size of yours. Everything below happens with your own hands — and all of it fits inside one book you take home, so none of it stops when you leave.

items.title: Watch first, touch second
items.body: Before anything else, a film — narrated in English. What koji actually is, what fermentation does, how it meets your gut microbiome, and how the seasonings you're about to make are made.

items.title: Meet four molds, not one
items.body: Yellow, black, white and red koji, side by side. One family, four different organisms, four completely different flavours. Most people in Japan have only ever met the yellow one.

items.title: Sow the spores yourself
items.body: You'll inoculate steamed rice with tane-koji — the seed spores — with your own hands. This is the step that turns rice into koji, and almost nobody outside a brewery has ever done it.

items.title: Koji-no-hana, under the microscope
items.body: Koji-no-hana — "the flower of koji" — is the white bloom that opens as the mold matures. You'll see it alive, magnified, with your own eyes. Not a diagram. The organism itself. This is the part everyone reaches for their phone.

items.title: Four seasonings, demonstrated
items.body: Shio-koji, ama-koji, shoyu-koji — and shoyu itself. Each one made in front of you, start to finish. You don't rush through them here: you go home with sealed koji and a soy sauce kit, and make all four in your own kitchen, at your own pace.

items.title: The tasting
items.body: Amazake, black-koji amazake, shio-koji and shoyu-koji, tasted side by side. The two amazake begin as the same rice. They taste nothing alike — and neither contains a grain of sugar. This is the one that surprises everybody.

items.title: Cook lunch, and learn to cook it again
items.body: We make lunch together using the seasonings you've just met — taught slowly enough that you can repeat it at home, not just eat it here.

items.title: Miso is not one thing
items.body: Climate, water and local culture have produced dozens of misos across Japan, and they barely resemble one another. You'll taste the difference rather than read about it.

items.title: The rare shelf
items.body: Chie's own cacao koji — made nowhere else in the world — alongside a run of ferments most people in Japan have never encountered.

blocks.title: Your fermentation journey continues
body: That is rather the point. You start it here, on this counter, and open it twelve months from now in your own kitchen. One afternoon in Tokyo, a year of it afterwards — and everything you need is in the one book you carry out the door.
list: RICE KOJI — sealed, ready to make shio-koji and amazake at home
AGED SOY SAUCE — a kit that keeps working for months in your own kitchen
KOJI GRAINS — to keep going after the first batch
TEXTBOOK INCLUDED — signed, and the whole session is in it
